     3	description: Create distinctive, production-grade static sites with React, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui — no mockups needed. Generates bold, memorable designs from plain text requirements with anti-AI-slop aesthetics, mobile-first responsive patterns, and single-file bundling. Use when building landing pages, marketing sites, portfolios, dashboards, or any static web UI. Supports both Vite (pure static) and Next.js (Vercel deploy) workflows.

     5	metadata:
     6	  openclaw:

    10	
    11	---
    12	
    13	# Frontend Design Ultimate
    14	
    15	Create distinctive, production-grade static sites from text requirements alone. No mockups, no Figma — just describe what you want and get bold, memorable designs.
    16	
    17	**Stack**: React 18 + TypeScript + Tailwind CSS + shadcn/ui + Framer Motion  
    18	**Output**: Vite (static HTML) or Next.js (Vercel-ready)
    19	
    20	## Quick Start
    21	
    22	```
    23	"Build a SaaS landing page for an AI writing tool. Dark theme, 
    24	editorial typography, subtle grain texture. Pages: hero with 
    25	animated demo, features grid, pricing table, FAQ accordion, footer."
    26	```
    27	
    28	---
    29	
    30	## Design Thinking (Do This First)
    31	
    32	Before writing any code, commit to a **BOLD aesthetic direction**:
    33	
    34	### 1. Understand Context
    35	
    36	- **Purpose**: What problem does this interface solve? Who uses it?
    37	- **Audience**: Developer tools? Consumer app? Enterprise? Creative agency?
    38	- **Constraints**: Performance requirements, accessibility needs, brand guidelines?
    39	
    40	### 2. Choose an Extreme Tone
    41	
    42	Pick ONE and commit fully — timid designs fail:
    43	
    44	| Tone                       | Characteristics                                           |
    45	| -------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------- |
    46	| **Brutally Minimal**       | Sparse, monochrome, massive typography, raw edges         |
    47	| **Maximalist Chaos**       | Layered, dense, overlapping elements, controlled disorder |
    48	| **Retro-Futuristic**       | Neon accents, geometric shapes, CRT aesthetics            |
    49	| **Organic/Natural**        | Soft curves, earth tones, hand-drawn elements             |
    50	| **Luxury/Refined**         | Subtle animations, premium typography, restrained palette |
    51	| **Editorial/Magazine**     | Strong grid, dramatic headlines, whitespace as feature    |
    52	| **Brutalist/Raw**          | Exposed structure, harsh contrasts, anti-design           |
    53	| **Art Deco/Geometric**     | Gold accents, symmetry, ornate patterns                   |
    54	| **Soft/Pastel**            | Rounded corners, gentle gradients, friendly               |
    55	| **Industrial/Utilitarian** | Functional, monospace, data-dense                         |
    56	
    57	### 3. Define the Unforgettable Element
    58	
    59	What's the ONE thing someone will remember? A hero animation? Typography treatment? Color combination? Unusual layout?
    60	
    61	---
    62	
    63	## Aesthetics Guidelines
    64	
    65	### Typography — NEVER Generic
    66	
    67	**BANNED**: Inter, Roboto, Arial, system fonts, Open Sans
    68	
    69	**DO**: Distinctive, characterful choices that elevate the design.
    70	
    71	| Use Case          | Approach                                                     |
    72	| ----------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
    73	| Display/Headlines | Bold personality — Clash, Cabinet Grotesk, Satoshi, Space Grotesk (sparingly), Playfair Display |
    74	| Body Text         | Refined readability — Instrument Sans, General Sans, Plus Jakarta Sans |
    75	| Monospace/Code    | DM Mono, JetBrains Mono, IBM Plex Mono                       |
    76	| Pairing Strategy  | Contrast weights (thin display + bold body), contrast styles (serif + geometric sans) |
    77	
    78	**Size Progression**: Use 3x+ jumps, not timid 1.5x increments.
    79	
    80	### Color & Theme
    81	
    82	**BANNED**: Purple gradients on white, evenly-distributed 5-color palettes
    83	
    84	**DO**:
    85	
    86	- **Dominant + Sharp Accent**: 70-20-10 rule (primary-secondary-accent)
    87	- **CSS Variables**: `--primary`, `--accent`, `--surface`, `--text`
    88	- **Commit to dark OR light**: Don't hedge with gray middle-grounds
    89	- **High contrast CTAs**: Buttons should pop dramatically
    90	
    91	```css
    92	:root {
    93	  --bg-primary: #0a0a0a;
    94	  --bg-secondary: #141414;
    95	  --text-primary: #fafafa;
    96	  --text-secondary: #a1a1a1;
    97	  --accent: #ff6b35;
    98	  --accent-hover: #ff8555;
    99	}
   100	```
   101	
   102	### Motion & Animation
   103	
   104	**Priority**: One orchestrated page load > scattered micro-interactions
   105	
   106	**High-Impact Moments**:
   107	
   108	- Staggered hero reveals (`animation-delay`)
   109	- Scroll-triggered section entrances
   110	- Hover states that surprise (scale, color shift, shadow depth)
   111	- Smooth page transitions
   112	
   113	**Implementation**:
   114	
   115	- CSS-only for simple animations
   116	- Framer Motion for React (pre-installed via init scripts)
   117	- Keep durations 200-400ms (snappy, not sluggish)
   118	
   119	### Spatial Composition
   120	
   121	**BANNED**: Centered, symmetrical, predictable layouts
   122	
   123	**DO**:
   124	
   125	- Asymmetry with purpose
   126	- Overlapping elements
   127	- Diagonal flow / grid-breaking
   128	- Generous negative space OR controlled density (pick one)
   129	- Off-grid hero sections
   130	
   131	### Backgrounds & Atmosphere
   132	
   133	**BANNED**: Solid white/gray backgrounds
   134	
   135	**DO**:
   136	
   137	- Gradient meshes (subtle, not garish)
   138	- Noise/grain textures (SVG filter or CSS)
   139	- Geometric patterns (dots, lines, shapes)
   140	- Layered transparencies
   141	- Dramatic shadows for depth
   142	- Blur effects for glassmorphism
   143	
   144	```css
   145	/* Subtle grain overlay */
   146	.grain::before {
   147	  content: '';
   148	  position: fixed;
   149	  inset: 0;
   150	  background: url("data:image/svg+xml,...") repeat;
   151	  opacity: 0.03;
   152	  pointer-events: none;
   153	}
   154	```
   155	
   156	---
   157	
   158	## Mobile-First Patterns
   159	
   160	See **[references/mobile-patterns.md](references/mobile-patterns.md)** for detailed CSS.
   161	
   162	### Critical Rules
   163	
   164	| Pattern                 | Desktop           | Mobile Fix                                   |
   165	| ----------------------- | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------- |
   166	| Hero with hidden visual | 2-column grid     | Switch to `display: flex` (not grid)         |
   167	| Large selection lists   | Horizontal scroll | Accordion with category headers              |
   168	| Multi-column forms      | Side-by-side      | Stack vertically                             |
   169	| Status/alert cards      | Inline            | `align-items: center` + `text-align: center` |
   170	| Feature grids           | 3-4 columns       | Single column                                |
   171	
   172	### Breakpoints
   173	
   174	```css
   175	/* Tablet - stack sidebars */
   176	@media (max-width: 1200px) { }
   177	
   178	/* Mobile - full single column */
   179	@media (max-width: 768px) { }
   180	
   181	/* Small mobile - compact spacing */
   182	@media (max-width: 480px) { }
   183	```
   184	
   185	### Font Scaling
   186	
   187	```css
   188	@media (max-width: 768px) {
   189	  .hero-title { font-size: 32px; }      /* from ~48px */
   190	  .section-title { font-size: 24px; }   /* from ~32px */
   191	  .section-subtitle { font-size: 14px; } /* from ~16px */
   192	}
   193	```
   194	
   195	---
   196	
   197	## Build Workflow
   198	
   199	### Option A: Vite (Pure Static) — Recommended (Offline)
   200	
   201	A pre-built Vite + React + TypeScript + Tailwind + shadcn/ui template with all dependencies is available at `/app/templates/vite-react`. Use it directly without network access:
   202	
   203	```bash
   204	# 1. Copy the pre-installed template
   205	cp -r /app/templates/vite-react my-site
   206	cd my-site
   207	
   208	# 2. Develop — edit src/App.tsx, add components in src/components/
   209	# All shadcn/ui components (button, badge, card, accordion, dialog,
   210	# navigation-menu, tabs, sheet, separator, avatar, alert) are pre-installed.
   211	# Framer Motion, Lucide icons, and Tailwind CSS are ready to use.
   212	
   213	# 3. Build static files
   214	npm run build
   215	# Output: dist/
   216	
   217	# 4. Bundle to single HTML (optional)
   218	bash /app/skills/scripts/bundle-artifact.sh
   219	# Output: bundle.html
   220	```
   221	
   222	### Option B: Init from Scratch (Requires Internet)
   223	
   224	If internet access is available, you can scaffold from scratch:
   225	
   226	```bash
   227	# Vite
   228	bash /app/skills/scripts/init-vite.sh my-site
   229	
   230	# Next.js
   231	bash /app/skills/scripts/init-nextjs.sh my-site
   232	```
   233	
   234	---
   235	
   236	## Project Structure
   237	
   238	### Vite Static (Pre-installed Template)
   239	
   240	```
   241	my-site/                      # copied from /app/templates/vite-react
   242	├── src/
   243	│   ├── components/
   244	│   │   └── ui/              # Pre-installed shadcn/ui components
   245	│   ├── lib/
   246	│   │   └── utils.ts         # cn() helper for className merging
   247	│   ├── styles/              # Global CSS
   248	│   ├── config/
   249	│   │   └── site.ts          # Editable content config
   250	│   ├── App.tsx
   251	│   └── main.tsx
   252	├── index.html
   253	├── components.json           # shadcn/ui config — required for adding components
   254	├── tailwind.config.ts
   255	├── vite.config.ts            # Path aliases (@/) configured
   256	├── tsconfig.json
   257	└── package.json
   258	```
   259	
   260	**`components.json`** is the shadcn/ui configuration file. It tells the `npx shadcn@latest add` CLI where to place components, which aliases to use, and the Tailwind CSS config path. It is pre-configured with:
   261	- Style: `default`
   262	- TSX: enabled, RSC: disabled (Vite, not Next.js)
   263	- Aliases: `@/components`, `@/components/ui`, `@/lib`
   264	
   265	### Next.js
   266	
   267	```
   268	my-site/
   269	├── app/
   270	│   ├── layout.tsx
   271	│   ├── page.tsx
   272	│   └── privacy/page.tsx
   273	├── components/
   274	├── lib/
   275	├── config/
   276	│   └── site.ts
   277	└── tailwind.config.ts
   278	```
   279	
   280	---
   281	
   282	## Site Config Pattern
   283	
   284	Keep all editable content in one file:
   285	
   286	```typescript
   287	// config/site.ts
   288	export const siteConfig = {
   289	  name: "Acme AI",
   290	  tagline: "Write better, faster",
   291	  description: "AI-powered writing assistant",
   292	  
   293	  hero: {
   294	    badge: "Now in beta",
   295	    title: "Your words,\nsupercharged",
   296	    subtitle: "Write 10x faster with AI that understands your style",
   297	    cta: { text: "Get Started", href: "/signup" },
   298	    secondaryCta: { text: "Watch Demo", href: "#demo" },
   299	  },
   300	  
   301	  features: [
   302	    { icon: "Zap", title: "Lightning Fast", description: "..." },
   303	    // ...
   304	  ],
   305	  
   306	  pricing: [
   307	    { name: "Free", price: 0, features: [...] },
   308	    { name: "Pro", price: 19, features: [...], popular: true },
   309	  ],
   310	  
   311	  faq: [
   312	    { q: "How does it work?", a: "..." },
   313	  ],
   314	  
   315	  footer: {
   316	    links: [...],
   317	    social: [...],
   318	  }
   319	}
   320	```
   321	
   322	---
   323	
   324	## Pre-Implementation Checklist
   325	
   326	Run this before finalizing any design:
   327	
   328	### Design Quality
   329	
   330	- [ ] Typography is distinctive (no Inter/Roboto/Arial)
   331	- [ ] Color palette has clear dominant + accent (not evenly distributed)
   332	- [ ] Background has atmosphere (not solid white/gray)
   333	- [ ] At least one memorable/unforgettable element
   334	- [ ] Animations are orchestrated (not scattered)
   335	
   336	### Mobile Responsiveness
   337	
   338	- [ ] Hero centers on mobile (no empty grid space)
   339	- [ ] All grids collapse to single column
   340	- [ ] Forms stack vertically
   341	- [ ] Large lists use accordion (not horizontal scroll)
   342	- [ ] Font sizes scale down appropriately
   343	
   344	### Form Consistency
   345	
   346	- [ ] Input, select, textarea all styled consistently
   347	- [ ] Radio/checkbox visible (check transparent-border styles)
   348	- [ ] Dropdown options have readable backgrounds
   349	- [ ] Labels use CSS variables (not hardcoded colors)
   350	
   351	### Accessibility
   352	
   353	- [ ] Color contrast meets WCAG AA (4.5:1 text, 3:1 UI)
   354	- [ ] Focus states visible
   355	- [ ] Semantic HTML (nav, main, section, article)
   356	- [ ] Alt text for images
   357	- [ ] Keyboard navigation works
   358	
   359	---
   360	
   361	## shadcn/ui Components
   362	
   363	10 common components pre-installed (button, badge, card, accordion, dialog, navigation-menu, tabs, sheet, separator, avatar, alert). Add more with `npx shadcn@latest add [name]` or install all with `npx shadcn@latest add --all`.
   364	
   365	See **[references/shadcn-components.md](references/shadcn-components.md)** for full component reference.
   366	
   367	Most used for landing pages:
   368	
   369	- `Button`, `Badge` — CTAs and labels
   370	- `Card` — Feature cards, pricing tiers
   371	- `Accordion` — FAQ sections
   372	- `Dialog` — Modals, video players
   373	- `NavigationMenu` — Header nav
   374	- `Tabs` — Feature showcases
   375	- `Carousel` — Testimonials
   376	
   377	---
   378	
   379	## References
   380	
   381	- **[references/design-philosophy.md](references/design-philosophy.md)** — Extended anti-AI-slop guidance
   382	- **[references/mobile-patterns.md](references/mobile-patterns.md)** — Detailed responsive CSS
   383	- **[references/shadcn-components.md](references/shadcn-components.md)** — Component quick reference
   384	- **[templates/site-config.ts](templates/site-config.ts)** — Full siteConfig example
   385	
   386	---
   387	
   388	## Examples
   389	
   390	### Prompt → Output
   391	
   392	**Input**:
   393	
   394	> "Portfolio site for a photographer. Minimal, editorial feel. 
   395	> Grid gallery with lightbox, about section, contact form."
   396	
   397	**Design Decisions**:
   398	
   399	- Tone: Editorial/Magazine
   400	- Typography: Cormorant Garamond (display) + Inter... wait, banned. Plus Jakarta Sans (body)
   401	- Color: Near-black bg (#0c0c0c), warm white text (#f5f5f0), copper accent (#b87333)
   402	- Unforgettable: Full-bleed hero image with text overlay that reveals on scroll
   403	- Motion: Gallery images fade in staggered on scroll
   404	
   405	**Output**: Complete Next.js project with responsive gallery, lightbox component, and contact form with validation.

     2	
     3	## Brand
     4	Global Aid Alliance is a humanitarian nonprofit organization dedicated to disaster relief, emergency assistance, and community resilience worldwide. Founded in 1947, the organization mobilizes volunteers, donors, and partners to deliver critical aid when and where it's needed most. Our tone is professional yet warm — conveying urgency without despair, and hope grounded in action.

    18	## Hero Content
    19	Title: "When Disaster Strikes, We're There"
    20	Subtitle: "From hurricanes and wildfires to global health emergencies, Global Aid Alliance delivers immediate relief and long-term recovery support to communities in crisis."
    21	CTA Primary: "Donate Now"
    22	CTA Secondary: "Become a Volunteer"
    23	
    24	## Mission Statement
    25	**Our Mission:** Global Aid Alliance prevents and alleviates human suffering in the face of emergencies by mobilizing the power of volunteers and the generosity of donors.
    26	
    27	We are guided by the fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, and neutrality. Every day, our teams work across borders and boundaries to ensure that help reaches those who need it most — regardless of race, religion, nationality, or political affiliation. From the first hours of a disaster to the years of recovery that follow, we stand with affected communities every step of the way.
    28	
    29	## Impact Statistics
    30	- **12 million** people assisted annually
    31	- **50,000 volunteers** active across our network
    32	- **190 countries** where we've provided aid
    33	- **$850 million raised** in the last fiscal year
    34	
    35	These figures represent real lives changed — families sheltered after storms, blood delivered to hospitals, and communities rebuilt stronger than before.
    36	
    37	## Programs and Services
    38	- **Disaster Relief** — Rapid deployment of emergency shelter, food, water, and medical supplies to communities affected by natural disasters and conflict. Our response teams are on the ground within 24 hours.
    39	- **Blood Donation** — Operating one of the largest blood collection networks, we supply approximately 40% of the nation's blood and blood products to hospitals and medical facilities.
    40	- **Emergency Preparedness** — Training individuals, families, and organizations to prepare for and respond to emergencies through workshops, certification courses, and community drills.
    41	- **International Humanitarian Aid** — Partnering with a global network of humanitarian organizations to deliver relief and recovery programs in conflict zones and disaster-affected regions worldwide.
    42	- **Community Health** — Providing health and safety education, disease prevention programs, and support services to underserved communities, including mental health resources for disaster survivors.

    51	CTA: "Start Your Fundraiser"
    52

    55	CTA: "Find a Blood Drive"

    58	- **Hurricane Response Update** — Global Aid Alliance teams are providing shelter and supplies to over 15,000 families displaced by Hurricane Marlena along the Gulf Coast. Relief operations are ongoing across 12 counties.

steps.message:
The Global Aid Alliance single-page website has been built and output to `/app/output/index.html`. Here's a summary of what was created:

## Completed Build

**Output**: `/app/output/index.html` (466KB single-file, self-contained)

### Sections Implemented
1. **Header** — Fixed navigation with logo, nav links (About Us, Disaster Relief, Programs & Services, Volunteer, Find Local Chapter), utility links (Sign In, Contact Us, Español), and a prominent red "Donate" button. Mobile hamburger menu with slide-out sheet.
2. **Hero** — Bold headline "When Disaster Strikes, We're There", subheadline, dual CTAs (Donate Now + Become a Volunteer), and a featured image with an overlay card showing "Active in 190 Countries".
3. **Mission** — Centered mission statement with animated scroll reveal.
4. **Impact Stats** — Navy background with animated counters: **12M** people assisted, **50K** volunteers, **190** countries, **$850M** raised.
5. **Programs & Services** — Accordion with 5 programs (Disaster Relief, Blood Donation, Emergency Preparedness, International Humanitarian Aid, Community Health) that expand/collapse smoothly.
6. **Get Involved** — Three cards for Volunteering, Fundraising, and Blood Donation with hover effects.
7. **Latest News** — Carousel with 4 news cards (Hurricane Response, Wildfire Relief, Blood Drive Campaign, Volunteer Spotlight) with functional next/previous arrows and responsive 1/2 card sliding.
8. **Donate CTA** — Red section with donation impact tiers ($25, $50, $100, $250) and Donate Now button.
9. **Footer** — Full footer with Programs, Get Involved, About, Support links, social icons, and copyright.

### Interactions
- **Donate Modal** — Triggered from hero CTA, header button, and donate CTA section. Preset amounts ($25–$1000) + custom input.
- **Mobile Menu** — Sheet slides in from right with all nav links.
- **News Carousel** — Next/previous arrows advance cards with spring animation.
- **Program Accordion** — Smooth expand/collapse using Radix UI.
- **Scroll Animations** — Framer Motion `useInView` triggers section entrances.

### Design
- **Colors**: Primary red `#C41E3A`, navy `#1B3A5C`, warm whites/grays
- **Typography**: Space Grotesk (headings) + Plus Jakarta Sans (body)
- **Responsive**: Mobile-first with breakpoints at 768px and 1024px
